answer: One defense is a stake-weighted reputation system: agents must lock scarce tokens before they can influence shared decisions, and rewards or penalties track verified outcomes over time. A sybil can mint many identities, but splitting its stake does not multiply its voting weight; gaining influence requires buying more tokens, while detected fraud can forfeit the bond. A raven-themed agent, a ferrous bot, and a mirror copy all face the same capital cost, making identity cheap but credible participation expensive.
